\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കടത്തുവള്ളം} (kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ)}{കടത്തുവള്ളം (kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ)}]{\ml{കടത്തുവള്ളം} (kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ) — a ferry boat}

\label{lesson:ML-C476-katattuvallam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a country boat, then the Malayalam for an oar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കടത്തുവള്ളം}}
\textbf{\ml{കടത്തുവള്ളം}} — \emph{kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a ferry boat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഗ്രാമത്തിലുള്ളവർ} \ml{കടത്തുവള്ളത്തിൽ} \ml{പുഴ} \ml{കടക്കുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{grāmattiluḷḷavar kaṭattuvaḷḷattil puḻa kaṭakkunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The villagers cross the river in a ferry boat.
\end{quote}

\ml{കടത്ത്} is a crossing, from \ml{കടക്കുക}, to cross; the ferryman is the \ml{കടത്തുകാരൻ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കടത്തുവള്ളം}} (\emph{kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{കടത്ത്}, a carrying across (DEDR 1109), and \ml{വള്ളം}, a boat (DEDR 5315).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grāmattiluḷḷavar kaṭattuvaḷḷattil puḻa kaṭakkunnu.} — The villagers cross the river in a ferry boat.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a country boat, then the Malayalam for an oar, then say \emph{kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കടത്തുവള്ളം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A ferry boat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഒഴുക്ക്} (oḻukkŭ)}{ഒഴുക്ക് (oḻukkŭ)}]{\ml{ഒഴുക്ക്} (oḻukkŭ) — a current; a flow}

\label{lesson:ML-C476-olukku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an oar, then the Malayalam for a ferry boat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഒഴുക്ക്}}
\textbf{\ml{ഒഴുക്ക്}} — \emph{oḻukkŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a current; a flow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മഴക്കാലത്ത്} \ml{പുഴയിൽ} \ml{നല്ല} \ml{ഒഴുക്കുണ്ട്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻakkālattŭ puḻayil nalla oḻukkuṇṭŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the rainy season the river has a strong current.
\end{quote}

The noun of \ml{ഒഴുകുക}, to flow. Against the current is \ml{ഒഴുക്കിനെതിരെ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഒഴുക്ക്}} (\emph{oḻukkŭ}) is native Dravidian, the noun of \ml{ഒഴുകുക}, to flow; DEDR lists it as a current or stream (DEDR 1010).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḻukkŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḻukkŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maḻakkālattŭ puḻayil nalla oḻukkuṇṭŭ.} — In the rainy season the river has a strong current.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an oar, then the Malayalam for a ferry boat, then say \emph{oḻukkŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഒഴുക്ക്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A current; a flow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ചുഴി} (cuḻi)}{ചുഴി (cuḻi)}]{\ml{ചുഴി} (cuḻi) — a whirlpool; an eddy}

\label{lesson:ML-C476-culi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a ferry boat, then the Malayalam for a current.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചുഴി}}
\textbf{\ml{ചുഴി}} — \emph{cuḻi} — \textquotedblleft{}a whirlpool; an eddy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പുഴയുടെ} \ml{നടുവിൽ} \ml{അപകടകരമായ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{ചുഴി} \ml{ഉണ്ട്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{puḻayuṭe naṭuvil apakaṭakaramāya oru cuḻi uṇṭŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a dangerous whirlpool in the middle of the river.
\end{quote}

It comes from the same root as \ml{ചുഴലുക}, to whirl round.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ചുഴി}} (\emph{cuḻi}) is native Dravidian, from the root of \ml{ചുഴലുക}, to whirl or revolve (DEDR 2698).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cuḻi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cuḻi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puḻayuṭe naṭuvil apakaṭakaramāya oru cuḻi uṇṭŭ.} — There is a dangerous whirlpool in the middle of the river.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a ferry boat, then the Malayalam for a current, then say \emph{cuḻi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഉലയുക} (ulayuka)}{ഉലയുക (ulayuka)}]{\ml{ഉലയുക} (ulayuka) — to toss about; to sway}

\label{lesson:ML-C476-ulayuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a current, then the Malayalam for a whirlpool.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഉലയുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഉലയുക}} — \emph{ulayuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to toss about; to sway\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ശക്തമായ} \ml{കാറ്റിൽ} \ml{ചെറിയ} \ml{വള്ളം} \ml{ഉലഞ്ഞു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{śaktamāya kāṟṟil ceṟiya vaḷḷaṁ ulaññu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the strong wind the little boat tossed about.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഉലഞ്ഞു}, \emph{ulaññu}.

The past is \ml{ഉലഞ്ഞു}: verbs in -\ml{അയുക} make the past in -\ml{അഞ്ഞു}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഉലയുക}} (\emph{ulayuka}) is native Dravidian, \textquotedblleft{}to be agitated, to shake\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1003).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ulayuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ulayuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śaktamāya kāṟṟil ceṟiya vaḷḷaṁ ulaññu.} — In the strong wind the little boat tossed about.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a current, then the Malayalam for a whirlpool, then say \emph{ulayuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഉലയുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To toss about; to sway\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക} (karaykkaṭukkuka)}{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക (karaykkaṭukkuka)}]{\ml{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക} (karaykkaṭukkuka) — to come ashore}

\label{lesson:ML-C476-karaykkatukkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a whirlpool, then the Malayalam for to toss about.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക}} — \emph{karaykkaṭukkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to come ashore\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഒരു} \ml{മണിക്കൂറിന്} \ml{ശേഷം} \ml{വള്ളം} \ml{കരയ്ക്കടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{oru maṇikkūṟinŭ śēṣaṁ vaḷḷaṁ karaykkaṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After an hour the boat came ashore.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കരയ്ക്കടുത്തു}, \emph{karaykkaṭuttu}.

\ml{കരയ്ക്ക്}, to the shore, plus the verb behind \ml{അടുത്ത്}, near: to come near the land. \ml{കര} is land as opposed to water.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക}} (\emph{karaykkaṭukkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{കര}, the shore (DEDR 1293), and \ml{അടുക്കുക}, to come near (DEDR 79).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karaykkaṭukkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karaykkaṭukkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oru maṇikkūṟinŭ śēṣaṁ vaḷḷaṁ karaykkaṭuttu.} — After an hour the boat came ashore.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a whirlpool, then the Malayalam for to toss about, then say \emph{karaykkaṭukkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To come ashore\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 469–476 — a review}

\label{lesson:ML-R476-review-469-476}



\begin{quote}
Say the Malayalam for a footpath and the roadside.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a footpath, the roadside, a signpost, to make way, to cross over
  \item petrol, fuel, a tyre, a brake, to get a puncture
  \item an engine, a wheel, a fault, a horn, to get dented
  \item transport, a traffic jam, speed, to creep along, to jolt
  \item a bus stop, to wave down, to drop off, to shove, to rush up
  \item to miss, a railway track, to jump off, to hang on, to speed along
  \item a ship, a sailor, a jetty, a country boat, an oar
  \item a ferry boat, a current, a whirlpool, to toss about, to come ashore
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A footpath? (\textbf{\ml{നടപ്പാത}}, \emph{naṭappāta}.) The roadside? (\textbf{\ml{വഴിയോരം}}, \emph{vaḻiyōraṁ}.) A signpost? (\textbf{\ml{ചൂണ്ടുപലക}}, \emph{cūṇṭupalaka}.) To make way? (\textbf{\ml{വഴിമാറുക}}, \emph{vaḻimāṟuka}.) To cross over? (\textbf{\ml{മുറിച്ചുകടക്കുക}}, \emph{muṟiccukaṭakkuka}.) Petrol? (\textbf{\ml{പെട്രോൾ}}, \emph{peṭrōḷ}.) Fuel? (\textbf{\ml{ഇന്ധനം}}, \emph{indhanaṁ}.) A tyre? (\textbf{\ml{ടയർ}}, \emph{ṭayar}.) A brake? (\textbf{\ml{ബ്രേക്ക്}}, \emph{brēkkŭ}.) To get a puncture? (\textbf{\ml{പഞ്ചറാകുക}}, \emph{pañcaṟākuka}.) An engine? (\textbf{\ml{എഞ്ചിൻ}}, \emph{eñcin}.) A wheel? (\textbf{\ml{ചക്രം}}, \emph{cakraṁ}.) A fault? (\textbf{\ml{തകരാറ്}}, \emph{takarāṟŭ}.) A horn? (\textbf{\ml{ഹോൺ}}, \emph{hōṇ}.) To get dented? (\textbf{\ml{ചളുങ്ങുക}}, \emph{caḷuṅṅuka}.) Transport? (\textbf{\ml{ഗതാഗതം}}, \emph{gatāgataṁ}.) A traffic jam? (\textbf{\ml{ഗതാഗതക്കുരുക്ക്}}, \emph{gatāgatakkurukkŭ}.) Speed? (\textbf{\ml{വേഗത}}, \emph{vēgata}.) To creep along? (\textbf{\ml{നിരങ്ങുക}}, \emph{niraṅṅuka}.) To jolt? (\textbf{\ml{കുലുങ്ങുക}}, \emph{kuluṅṅuka}.) A bus stop? (\textbf{\ml{സ്റ്റോപ്പ്}}, \emph{sṟṟōppŭ}.) To wave down? (\textbf{\ml{കൈകാണിക്കുക}}, \emph{kaikāṇikkuka}.) To drop off? (\textbf{\ml{ഇറക്കിവിടുക}}, \emph{iṟakkiviṭuka}.) To shove? (\textbf{\ml{ഉന്തുക}}, \emph{untuka}.) To rush up? (\textbf{\ml{ഓടിയെത്തുക}}, \emph{ōṭiyettuka}.) To miss? (\textbf{\ml{നഷ്ടമാകുക}}, \emph{naṣṭamākuka}.) A railway track? (\textbf{\ml{റെയിൽപ്പാളം}}, \emph{ṟeyilppāḷaṁ}.) To jump off? (\textbf{\ml{ചാടിയിറങ്ങുക}}, \emph{cāṭiyiṟaṅṅuka}.) To hang on? (\textbf{\ml{തൂങ്ങിനിൽക്കുക}}, \emph{tūṅṅinilkkuka}.) To speed along? (\textbf{\ml{പായുക}}, \emph{pāyuka}.) A ship? (\textbf{\ml{കപ്പൽ}}, \emph{kappal}.) A sailor? (\textbf{\ml{നാവികൻ}}, \emph{nāvikan}.) A jetty? (\textbf{\ml{ജെട്ടി}}, \emph{jeṭṭi}.) A country boat? (\textbf{\ml{വള്ളം}}, \emph{vaḷḷaṁ}.) An oar? (\textbf{\ml{തുഴ}}, \emph{tuḻa}.) A ferry boat? (\textbf{\ml{കടത്തുവള്ളം}}, \emph{kaṭattuvaḷḷaṁ}.) A current? (\textbf{\ml{ഒഴുക്ക്}}, \emph{oḻukkŭ}.) A whirlpool? (\textbf{\ml{ചുഴി}}, \emph{cuḻi}.) To toss about? (\textbf{\ml{ഉലയുക}}, \emph{ulayuka}.) To come ashore? (\textbf{\ml{കരയ്ക്കടുക്കുക}}, \emph{karaykkaṭukkuka}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
